inputs.declared_question: How does a place for asynchronous reply move from an experiential proposition into a bounded instrument and a working artifact?

source_facts.claim: FN-35 describes a finite collage correspondence where seven arrivals preserve a changing shared surface and end as an interactive relic.
source_facts.locator: What the canvas holds; The speed of making, the time of answering; An ending that can still be encountered

cartographer.inference: I-005 is a direct implementation of the encounter proposed in FN-35, and A-005 is the current working embodiment of I-005. These relations are strong because the exact publications name one another and distinguish proposition, conduct, technical construction, and artifact evidence.
cartographer.uncertainty: The prototype has not yet demonstrated a completed interpersonal exchange, whether seven arrivals serve participants well, or how a future shared service can preserve addressed turns without centralizing private correspondence.
cartographer.attribution: All facts are attributed to the exact September 6 Cyberdelic OS publications. No private repository or conversation was read beyond what those public records themselves disclose.
cartographer.stop_reason: The bounded internal continuity yielded two strong implementation proposals. A separate Builder Note relation was left for a later finite turn rather than filling every available connection.
